old: This word points to a female figure once linked to a mound said to house otherworldly folk.
It comes from Irish words meaning 'woman' and 'fairy mound.'
Its ancestor is Old Irish ben síde — a phrase almost identical in shape to the English word it produced in 1771.
clues: This spirit of Irish folklore was named for where it was believed to live, not for what it did: its original name meant 'woman of the fairy mound.'
Not the ghost of someone who died, she is a fairy woman whose eerie nighttime wailing is said to warn a family that one of them will soon die.
When someone lets out a piercing, unearthly scream, people often say they are shrieking or howling 'like a ___.'
